text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — customer asked what audit events they can see when they use scoped read-only tokens. Are admin-only events (role changes, KMS key ops) included for tenant admins only? We need clarifying guidance for SOC customers.

Keith Park: Good q. Current schema tags events with tenant_id but we also have an actor_role field. Important: admin-level ops are emitted but access filtered at query layer. That hasn't been validated for scoped tokens.

Tim O'Neill: infra note — scoped tokens are enforced by the auth proxy, but the audit pipeline still stores raw events in the central ES cluster. Need to check access controls and encryption-in-flight for those indexes.

Jen Morales: Product: customers expect a "customer_audit_events" export that excludes org-level ops from infra. We should formalize what 'admin' means in the product contract (tenant_admin vs org_admin vs infra).

Sara Gupta: Security suggestion — add event.visibility with enumerated values like [tenant_admin, org_admin, infra] in the schema. Also add event.redaction_policy = pii|partial|none so exports can show what was redacted.

Keith Park: +1 on visibility. For backcompat, if the field is missing assume visibility=tenant_admin. Also add a versioned field audit_schema_v so consumers can migrate.

Maria Chen: Any KMS-specific events leak key identifiers? We currently log kms.key_id and operation. For SOC2 customers, probably need to avoid raw key IDs in customer-facing exports.

Tim O'Neill: Agree. Suggest we stop logging raw kms.key_id and instead log kms.key_id_sha256 plus kms.key_id_redacted boolean. Do NOT log key material. Also ensure the pipeline never serializes plaintext key identifiers into customer exports.

devsec-bot: NOTE: Draft RFC created at /docs/rfcs/audit-schema-v2.md — reviewers @keith, @sara. Includes visibility, redaction_policy, audit_schema_v and example migration steps.

Olivia Khan: Support: customers ask to see "who did what" within their tenant. Members should only see events they or their teammates generated; admins should be able to filter for role changes, key ops (redacted). Scoped tokens for members must not allow read access to org_admin events.

Jen Morales: UX ask — add an 'event.acted_on_behalf_of' field to show service account impersonation so customers can trace robot actions. Small and useful for investigations.

Sara Gupta: Also propose adding a validation layer in ingestion that tags or rejects events whose visibility doesn't align with actor_role. Example rule: if actor_role=member and event.type in [role_change, policy_update] -> set visibility=org_admin and route to secure bucket rather than customer export.

Keith Park: Implementation details: ingestion lambda should canonicalize actor (canonical_actor_id), sign events with an ingestion signature, and add disclosure_flags. We'll need contract tests: sample events -> expected visibility + redaction.

Maria Chen: For rollout: create a migration that adds default values for missing visibility and audit_schema_v, and a feature flag to enable strict validation. Canary on Dedicated customers first, then hosted.

Tim O'Neill: Ops plan — add per-tenant indexing alias, apply RBAC at query time using ES search templates that inject tenant-scoped filters based on token claims (token.tenant_id + token.scopes). Also ensure encryption-at-rest for customer audit exports.

Olivia Khan: Customer-facing validation: include a validation_results array in exports that lists redactions and reason codes (e.g., "redacted_kms_key_id:policy"). That will reduce support churn.

Maria Chen: Action items: Keith to write RFC + schema PR, Tim to prototype kms hashing and per-tenant aliasing, Sara to update threat model + contract tests, Olivia to draft customer messaging and export examples. Can we aim for EOD Friday for the RFC draft? :calendar:

Keith Park: I'm on it. Will ping the thread when PR is up. :thumbsup:

Tim O'Neill: I'll put a quick prototype in the infra-sandbox repo and link it here.

Sara Gupta: I'll add the validation rules to the ingestion playbook and start the contract test matrix.

Olivia Khan: I'll draft email + portal copy that explains what customers will see and why some fields are redacted.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. If anyone spots an edge case: cross-tenant roles, delegated org-admins, or partner service accounts — call it out here.

Keith Park: One more edge case — backup/restore flows that replay events: ensure replayed events preserve original visibility and are not reclassified. Add replay marker to the schema (event.replay_marker).

Maria Chen: Good call. Add that to the RFC.

devsec-bot: Reminder: add test vectors for replay + visibility and include kms.key_id hashing in testdata.
